title: Consumer feedback papertrail and microfix blueprint — Oct 2026 digest
summary: Compact compilation of recent frontline feedback (Sep 15–Oct 1 2026), distilled into actionable microfixes and a small set of higher-effort asks. Prioritization favors low-risk ops changes that improve latency and predictability for mid-market customers using Dedicated and Private modes.
high_level_findings: Recurring customer theme: unpredictable tail latency during bursty traffic on Dedicated pools; most customers report spikes during short-lived user flows rather than steady sustained load.
KV cache confusion: several customers misinterpret 'prefix caching' behavior when using multi-turn chat with dynamic system prompts; this has led to redundant token generation and higher costs.
Fallback model behavior is opaque: customers want explicit signal/metrics when a request was served by a lower‑cost fallback model (and a knob to prefer quality over cost per route).
Quick wins outweigh long-run investments for >60% of incoming asks in this window; customers prefer small, documented mitigations they can enable client-side while we pursue longer rollouts.
detailed_requests: Priority A — Dedicated tail-smoothing: request for a configuration flag that soft-limits concurrent model initializations within a pool (example customer: FinSaaS). Impact: reduces 95–99th percentile latency at short bursts. Estimate: small runtime change + one-week ops validation. Engineering note: may interact with burst capacity; needs SRE signoff.

Priority A — KV cache visibility: expose per-request header/response flag that indicates whether prefix/KV cache hit occurred and approximate saved tokens. Customer quote: 'We can do less defensive prompting if we know cache helps us.' Impact: low effort on API surface, big UX win for customers optimizing prompts.

Priority B — Fallback transparency toggle: add boolean on route config to attach 'served-by' metadata when automatic fallback happens; optionally emit an event to the console with reason. Example use: ecommerce recommendation engines wanting auditability. Impact: moderate; requires schema extension and docs.

Priority B — Streamed partial-rollbacks for model rollouts: allow canary responses to be streamed with a parallel non-streaming baseline for A/B comparison (customer: HealthTech). This helps detect quality regressions quickly. Impact: higher engineering scope; aligns with rollout roadmap.

Priority C — Embedding size selector: customers using embeddings for semantic search want an easy switch between 384/768 dims with explicit cost delta shown in console. Impact: product+billing change, modest eng work; medium priority.
quick_fixes: Add a short KB note and SDK snippet demonstrating defensive prompt patterns that avoid regenerations when KV cache misses are expected — immediate docs push, low effort.
Temporarily add a 'cache-suspected' boolean in our diagnostic logs for teams with open tickets to speed triage (ops-only feature).
Adjust default autoscale cooldown to favor warm standby in Dedicated pools for customers flagged as latency-sensitive (can be targeted via account flag).
Surface a lightweight cost-estimate tooltip in the Console when enabling model fallback on a route (explains expected token savings and quality tradeoffs).
risk_and_unknowns: Tail smoothing may increase baseline GPU utilization; for heavily cost-constrained customers this could be undesirable without an opt-out.
Exposing cache hits as a signal could leak intermediate prompt structure if customers store headers externally — we should document privacy considerations.
Some customers want deterministic 'served-by' guarantees; providing that across multi-region fallbacks could require capacity reservations we don't currently support.
Embeddings size toggle must coordinate with downstream index schemas in customer infra; we need migration guidance to avoid silently breaking searches.
customer-quotes: 'We see 200–400ms spikes during checkouts — it kills conversions.' — midsize marketplace CTO
'If I knew the cache hit-rate, I could safely simplify my prompt and drop 10% token spend.' — platform engineer at EdTech company
'Fallbacks are great but we need an audit trail when they happen for compliance reviews.' — security lead at healthcare customer
impact_estimates_and_rationale: KV cache visibility: impact high for prompt engineering velocity; estimated dev time 3–5 days to add headers + 2 days docs + 1 week of limited QA.
Tail-smoothing flag: medium impact on latency P95/P99; estimated 2 weeks of runtime changes + 1 week validation with 2 pilot customers.
Fallback transparency toggle: medium impact on trust/compliance for enterprise customers; estimated 1 sprint across API + console + alerts workstreams.
